pages.title: Read This First
pages.text: Hold a wand to see available inventory mana and focus. Check the formed core for base costs and the wand for its multipliers.$(br2)Aether and mana amounts use K (thousand), M (million), and B (billion). This guide records common rules; trust the readings on your core. Creative mode spends no resources.

pages.title: Two Resources
pages.text: Focus is your ability to control a spell. It belongs to the player and recovers naturally.$(br2)Mana belongs to items and does not regenerate. It needs an external supply. Damage, area, targets and duration mainly affect mana.

pages.title: Base Cost and Complexity
pages.text: Each cast costs:$(br2)F=5+10*C+0.625*C^2$(br2)5 is the fixed startup cost; C is total structural complexity. An entity effect contributes 0.1 and a modifier 0.05. Combine complexity before converting to focus once. Damage values and actual target counts do not change C.

pages.title: Simple and Complex Spells
pages.text: Using the same self selector and damage effects:$(br2)1 effect: C=0.3, about 8.06 focus.$(br)10 effects: C=1.2, 17.90 focus.$(br)50 effects: C=5.2, 73.90 focus.$(br2)More complex structures carry an increasing burden. Raising one damage value only increases mana.

pages.title: Loops
pages.text: Let C be body complexity and n the maximum repetitions. Loop complexity is:$(br2)0.2 + L(n)*C$(br2)L(n)=log2(1+n). For C=0.3 and n=10, loop complexity is about 1.238; combine it with the rest of the structure before calculating focus. Mana still counts every effect.

pages.title: Delays
pages.text: A delay adds 0.15+H(t) complexity, plus its action.$(br2)H(t)=0.05*log2(1+t/20), with t in ticks. Normally 20 ticks make a second. Repeated delays use the span from first to last repetition, rather than charging focus each tick.

pages.title: Branches
pages.text: Branch complexity is:$(br2)0.1+P+max(A,B)+0.25*min(A,B)$(br2)P is condition complexity; A and B are branch complexities. Preparing a fallback adds a small burden. Mana pays for the chosen branch, but reserves for the more expensive one.

pages.title: Damage Prices
pages.text: Ordinary damage costs, per target and attempt:$(br2)m(d)=500*d+12.5*d*d$(br2)Damage 4 costs 2.2K mana; 20 costs 15K; 100 costs 175000. Stronger single hits cost more per damage point. Damage types share the default price. Focus does not grow with d.

pages.title: Whole Mana Costs
pages.text: Effect fees accumulate before applying the wand multiplier. Total mana is rounded up to a whole number, as is the base mana shown on cores.$(br2)For example, startup 10 plus ten particles priced at 0.2 costs 12 mana. Startup plus one particle rounds 10.2 up to 11. Focus may still be fractional.

pages.title: Reserve, Then Settle
pages.text: Before starting, reserve enough mana from inventory and offhand containers to complete the spell. Insufficient mana prevents the cast without spending either resource.$(br2)A complete miss returns only 50% of unused reserves by default; the rest is lost. After a valid target attempt, unused reserves return in full. Startup, delivery, queries and damage attempts remain paid, even if a target resists. A failed casting condition still spends preparation focus and actual query fees.

pages.title: Missed Spell Losses
pages.text: If a spell ends with 1K unused mana, the default refund is 500 and the other 500 is lost. Startup, queries and effect fees already spent are not refunded.$(br2)Cosmetic spells, block spells and failed casting conditions are exempt by default. Different worlds may lose different amounts; watch what actually returns to your jars. Refunds round down to keep consumption whole.

pages.title: When Focus Runs Low
pages.text: With enough mana, a bounded spell may overdraw focus below zero and finish its delayed effects and projectiles.$(br2)No new spells can start until focus fully recovers. Channeling stops before its next pulse; effects already started are not undone.

pages.title: Focus Is Never Refunded
pages.text: Structural focus is paid once when the spell starts, regardless of target count. Missing, refunding mana or cancelling later effects never returns that focus.$(br2)The refund ratio affects item mana only. Even at a 100% mana refund, focus must recover normally, and overdraw still locks casting until it is full.

pages.title: Debt and Recovery
pages.text: After overdraw, the red bar shows remaining focus debt. Once it reaches zero, the recovery bar fills until focus is full and lockout ends. Recovery defaults to 10 per second: zero to maximum 100 takes about 10 seconds, with extra time for debt.$(br2)With maximum 100, Earth Spike Field costs about 136.98 and leaves -36.98. Full recovery takes about 13.7 seconds at normal tick speed. Not every glimmer remains visible in a dense burst, but the spell's effects and costs remain the same.

pages.title: Keep Your Effects
pages.text: A particle costs 0.2 mana and a sound 1; both add zero complexity. Purely decorative controls use 2% of normal complexity; decorative startup costs 10 mana.$(br2)Every separate cast still pays the fixed 5 focus. Adding effects to an existing spell does not add another startup cost.$(br2)A beautiful spell need not be an expensive one.

pages.title: Symbols in Effect Entries
pages.text: d: requested damage; v: speed; r: teleport distance; t: ticks; a: amplifier, where zero means level I; k: price factor, default 1.$(br2)Timed effects start at 20*t*(a+1)^2*k. Instant effects use 1K*(a+1)^2*k. Trust the actual readings on your core.

pages.title: Wands and Creative Mode
pages.text: Mana and focus each use the corresponding wand multiplier: 1 for the beginner wand and 0 for the creative wand.$(br2)In creative mode, all wands cast without resource costs or focus lockout. An infinite mana container in survival supplies unlimited mana, but an ordinary wand still spends focus.

pages.title: Selections and Limits
pages.text: Each selection affects at most 8 targets by default, nearest to its origin first. Reserves cover all 8 slots; settlement normally pays only for actual targets; a complete miss also loses part of the unused reserve.$(br2)Repetitions, range, lifetime and simultaneous casts also have limits. Unbounded costs or excessive settings prevent casting. Reduce the range or repetitions.

pages.title: Base Costs on Cores
pages.text: Core tooltips calculate base mana and focus from saved values, including local variables, loop indices, repetition counts, areas and effect levels.$(br2)Base prices assume one target and multipliers of 1. Additional targets, travel distance and future random values are not part of the fixed base.
